baseline_scope: Reuse all 88 actual completed 0.35 optimizer runs, initial observations and independent evaluation measurements. New baseline cases import the six saved 0.35 source modules, including objective-aware experiment planning. No observation repair enters this baseline.

policy.evidence: Paired constraint predictions made before each new optimizer observation; the research data fit both models but do not count as prior-adoption trials

evaluation.rule: Public evaluation coordinates and all final Program/GP predictions are frozen after each optimizer run. After every selected run is complete, a separate actual simulator stream supplies shared measurements and evaluator-only true constraint means. Evaluation calls never enter the controller and are reported separately.
evaluation.additional_requested_metrics: Record which experimental controls provide useful measured objective values, objective prediction errors on actual future observations, final objective-GP predictions on the same frozen independent controls when available, and the best measured point after the mechanism change. Preserve the original constraint Program/GP errors, confirmation and revision sequence, feasibility, and paid costs.

accounting: Research acquires 32 actual full objective/constraint vectors once per distinct initial task and shares them across both arms and same-task stable/change profiles. All loaded calls count toward each arm's N64. New revision questions replace ordinary optimizer calls inside the same remaining 32 calls; full history is retained. Historical reuse, new acquisition, extra model compute, and independent evaluation calls are separate.
metrics: final Program and active GP generalization MSE
common misfit, question, fresh validation, and scope adoption sequence
scope: All 88 previous cases are development. Three previously unused seeds each provide six ordinary confirmation cases (two noise levels and three profiles), one single-constraint-outlier control, and one single outlier followed by a real mechanism change. Stress groups remain separate. Every optimizer arm uses the same 32 initial plus 32 new actual calls.
reuse_accounting: Only the new arm reruns 88 development cases. Both arms run 18 fresh ordinary and six fresh stress cases (136 new optimizer runs, 4352 online calls). Initial research, its supplement, independent evaluation, and predictor-repair work are accounted separately.
baseline_revision_evidence: Keep the original four-observation batch size and nine-times-frozen-reference threshold. Nonoverlapping actual measurement batches reopen research when both models' batch MSE exceed the threshold and at least two individual rows exceed it for both models. The new scope starts at the earliest such counterexample and retains every subsequently paid row. Eight coverage calls and four fresh validation calls remain inside N64. No change labels, times, or truth values reach the controller.
research_initialization: Fresh initial data and executable programs use the saved 0.35 claim compiler. The existing public stratified completion rule supplies 32 actual vectors; both arms share these values. The new stress cases reuse their ordinary same-task noisy StatePolicy initialization.

baseline_method.unchanged: The 0.34 detector, actual anchor confirmation, constraint candidate compilation and competition, and training/future acceptance thresholds remain unchanged.
baseline_method.objective_model: Fit normalized affine and coordinate-additive quadratic objective programs using the current episode's paid full-vector observations. Select by leave-one-out prediction loss; retain frozen fold models. Prediction variance equals CV loss plus jackknife variance. This Gaussian expected-improvement proxy ranks actions and is not assumed to be a calibrated net-value estimator.
baseline_method.incumbent: The minimum paid objective in the current scope whose measured constraint satisfies the public constraint upper bound. No evaluator truth enters the controller. Without a feasible measured incumbent, each constraint candidate can offer its minimum predicted feasible objective point.
baseline_method.pool: Keep the existing public random and boundary pool. Add the analytic box-constrained minimum of the learned separable objective model and 33-point sweeps along every public coordinate through that learned minimum; no task-specific solution is supplied.
baseline_method.selection: Of four future validation controls, at most two use predicted feasibility and objective opportunity. Each constraint candidate offers its lowest predicted feasible objective point; choose the first offer by Gaussian expected improvement. Choose the second from the predicted-feasible pool by expected improvement times normalized squared distance to the first. Slots without positive opportunity return to disagreement selection. At least two controls retain disagreement times diversity. Missing objective data retains the original selector.
baseline_method.accounting: Charge all objective fits, held-out fit predictions, fold/pool objective predictions, and constraint predictions to the same existing compute budget. All selected controls consume the original N64 actual observations.

outlier_control: The actual simulator runs normally and its constraint output receives the frozen +1.0 observation disturbance on the thirteenth online call only. Objectives, future measurements, and evaluator truth remain unchanged. A report-only log records the disturbance; the runtime receives only ordinary measured outputs and public controls. The corresponding ordinary stable case receives no disturbance. Initial data and final evaluation measurements are shared with that stable case.

new_method.unchanged: The 0.35 joint confirmation trigger, frozen pre-observation predictions, real repeated control, candidate competition, objective-aware experiment selection, and genuine mechanism revision remain unchanged.
new_method.repair_evidence: Only after a same-point confirmation is not supported: at least one frozen original prediction has repeated-target squared error at most the frozen threshold, while squared difference between original and repeated targets exceeds twice that threshold. No simulator disturbance label or evaluator truth enters this decision.
new_method.predictor_repair: Retain snapshots of both constraint predictors and their constraint-specific HVD state before assimilating the questioned original observation. Restore those states and replay the actual repeated constraint measurement, excluding the rejected anchor only from constraint fitting and replication statistics. Preserve both objective measurements.
new_method.knowledge_scope: Do not replace the executable prior, open a new world scope, or erase history for an observation repair. Keep annotations linking the rejected anchor and its paid confirmation; exclude rejected constraint adoption evidence from subsequent decisions while preserving original evidence and costs.
new_method.accounting: All original and repeated observations remain in the full paid N64 ledger. Count predictor repairs, restored model state, snapshot work, replayed constraint updates, and rejected measurements still charged to the budget. There are no extra simulator calls for repair.

mixed_control: The StatePolicy simulator supplies one +1.0 constraint observation at global stage41 (online9), with unchanged objective and future observations. Starting at global stage45 (online13), both actual objective and constraint mechanisms switch to RZDT2. The runtime receives only public controls and ordinary simulator outputs; changes and disturbances are report-only. This asks whether observation repair preserves sensitivity to later drift.
